title: Use a constructor reference `Employee::new` to create employees from a stream of data.
shortTitle: Use a constructor reference Employee::new to create employees from a stream of data
keyPoints: Employee::new is a constructor reference that treats the constructor as a functional value
The compiler selects the constructor overload matching the target functional interface's signature
Function<String, Employee> matches a one-arg constructor; BiFunction matches two-arg
Cleaner than name -> new Employee(name) because it names the construction directly
Also used with toArray(Employee[]::new) to create typed arrays from streams
Use a lambda or static factory when validation or defaulting is needed during construction

s1_definition.oneliner: Employee::new is a factory reference: feed it data and it calls the matching constructor to build objects.
s1_definition.profdef:
- A **constructor reference** `Type::new` refers to a constructor as a functional value.
- The compiler matches the constructor whose parameter list fits the target functional interface.
- `Function<String, Employee>` matches a single-argument constructor.
- `BiFunction<String, String, Employee>` matches a two-argument constructor.
- Also used with **toArray(Type[]::new)** to build typed arrays.
s1_definition.analogy: Priya at the National Bank of India has a list of raw names and wants an employee record for each. Instead of writing 'take a name and build a new employee', she just points at the employee factory and feeds it names.

sections.s3_flow:
```text
  Stream<String>   ["Rajesh", "Priya", "Amit"]
       │
       │  .map(Employee::new)
       │
       │  Compiler matches:
       │  Employee(String name)  ← one-arg constructor
       ▼
  Stream<Employee>
  [Employee(Rajesh), Employee(Priya), Employee(Amit)]
       │
       │  .toArray(Employee[]::new)
       ▼
  Employee[]  ← typed array
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
A constructor reference treats a constructor as a functional value. Employee::new matched against Function<String, Employee> invokes the one-argument constructor, turning a stream of names into a stream of Employee objects. The compiler picks the overload whose parameters match the target functional interface.

At the National Bank of India, onboarding imports used Employee::new to lift raw holder names into domain objects, reading more cleanly than the equivalent lambda. Constructor references also pair with toArray(Employee[]::new) to produce typed arrays.

A bare constructor reference assumes the constructor alone fully builds the object. When validation or defaulting is needed, step back to a lambda or a static factory method.

Remember one sentence: Employee::new is a constructor reference that creates objects by matching the constructor overload to the target functional interface.
